newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank props up Jordan stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank props up Jordan stock exchange.

text.p: A slight rise in blue-chip Arab Bank ahead of its weekend annual shareholders meeting helped push Jordanian shares up on Wednesday despite a fall in heavily-traded Housing Bank.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index climbed 0.48 percent to end the week at 153.72 points after shares worth 552,000 dinars ($778,000) changed hands.

Arab Bank shares rose two dinars to 256 dinars ahead of Friday's annual general meeting. Investors hope the bank will shed light on its plans for a bonus share issue, which depends on ratification of a new law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.
Shares have fallen from 269 dinars two weeks ago on fears that the bonus share issue would be indefinitely delayed.

Housing Bank, Wednesday's most heavily traded share, fell 0.08 dinars to 4.80 dinars. Brokers said speculators who jumped in on Tuesday on the back of heavy institutional demand were offloading stock on Wednesday.
"Once they felt the demand was over they got out," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah.
Other heavily-traded stock included Jordan Industrial Reserves and Livestock and Poultry, which both eased slightly. Bank of Jordan closed unchanged at 2.80 dinars after trade worth 45,000 dinars.
Overall, 17 shares rose while another 17 fell and 11 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange rose 0.05 percent to 80.50 points, 3.47 percent down from the start of the year.
